chain.label: Grandfathered certification basis and ambiguous pretakeoff checklist
chain.trigger: because the Cessna 560XL was initially certificated 4 years before the parking brake indication amendment, there is no requirement for a cockpit indication if the parking brake is not fully released

chain.label: No parking brake annunciation; knob hidden from right-seat pilot
chain.trigger: lack of a 'no takeoff' annunciation warning that the parking brake was engaged, and lack of a checklist item to ensure the parking brake was fully released immediately before takeoff

caused_by.evidence: Textron continues to manufacture Cessna 560XL airplanes without a parking brake indication, including the XLS+ derivative model

chain.label: Hazards and dropping terrain beyond departure end of runway
chain.trigger: Potential hazards beyond the runway include steep slopes, fences, hills, buildings, bodies of water, and highways

chain.label: Parking brake not fully released before takeoff roll
chain.trigger: the airplane's parking brake valve and pull knob were in the set position, which indicated that the airplane's parking brake had likely not been fully released before the attempted takeoff

caused_by.evidence: the airplane's static and rolling takeoff checklists direct the pilot to 'release brakes,' but that item could be misinterpreted to refer only to the toe brakes
the pull knob is not visible to the right-seat pilot

chain.label: Crew did not recognize parking brake was still set
chain.trigger: without a parking brake indication, some Cessna 560XL pilots may not recognize that the parking brake is not fully released and attempt to take off

caused_by.evidence: The existence of a physical stimulus in the cockpit, such as a pull knob or indication, does not guarantee that the pilot will perceive an unsafe condition
he had not released the airplane's parking brake pull knob, which was located next to his left knee, before the takeoff roll

chain.label: Residual brake pressure created nose-down pitching moment preventing rotation at Vr
chain.trigger: the resulting retarding force at the wheel-runway interface creates a pitching moment that opposes airplane nose-up rotation... may overpower the elevator's ability to rotate the airplane nose up

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's failure to release the parking brake before attempting to initiate the takeoff, which produced an unexpected retarding force and airplane nose down pitching moment
the airplane had exceeded the speed required to take off (rotational speed or Vr) and did not lift off the ground in response to the pilot pulling the yoke aft

chain.label: Takeoff continued/rejected too late, past the point of safe stopping
chain.trigger: Once the airplanes reached this point in the takeoff sequence, they were beyond the point at which they could be stopped safely

caused_by.evidence: Also causal was the flight crew's delayed decision to abort the takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion

chain.label: Overran departure end of runway
chain.trigger: a Cessna 560XL airplane, N560AR, overran the departure end of the runway during the takeoff roll near Farmington, Connecticut

caused_by.evidence: If the takeoff is rejected after reaching Vr, the airplane may not be able to stop safely on the remaining runway
the flight crew's delayed decision to abort the takeoff, which resulted in a runway excursion

chain.label: Briefly airborne, pitched up, struck pole and ground
chain.trigger: after clearing the departure end of the runway and becoming briefly airborne, it pitched up then impacted a pole. After that, the airplane impacted the ground

caused_by.evidence: the airplane departed the runway, it was in a level attitude
the airplane rapidly pitched up once the terrain dropped away beyond the departure end of the runway

chain.label: Collided with building and was destroyed
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted the ground then a building and was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: it pitched up then impacted a pole. After that, the airplane impacted the ground then a building
Potential hazards beyond the runway include steep slopes, fences, hills, buildings

chain.label: Four occupants fatally injured; building occupants injured
chain.trigger: the two pilots and two passengers were fatally injured. One occupant of the building that was impacted sustained serious injury and three occupants sustained minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: impacted... a building and was destroyed, and the two pilots and two passengers were fatally injured
